title: Anal fissure surgery
summary: Learn more about anal fissures, their causes, symptoms, and how surgical intervention can bring long-term relief.
intro: An anal fissure is a small tear in the lining of the anus, often caused by passing hard or large stools. It leads to severe pain and bleeding during bowel movements.
While most fissures heal with conservative treatments, chronic cases may require surgical intervention to relieve the sphincter muscle and improve healing.
causes: Chronic constipation or hard stool passage
Fissures that do not respond to creams or medications
benefits: Lateral internal sphincterotomy is the most common surgical method. It has a high success rate (over 90%) and can provide rapid pain relief and improved healing.
